questions.passage: Is this a weed, Dad? Do I pull it out?
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'in a/the garden' — a child asking a parent about pulling out a weed implies they are gardening together. Reject answers with no connection to gardening; a joke/off-topic answer is acceptable ONLY if it still clearly names 'garden' as the location, otherwise reject.

questions.passage: The children took turns on the swings and slides.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'at a/the playground' (or 'a park'). Reject unrelated locations.

questions.passage: The clothes flapped in the breeze.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'on a clothesline/washing line' — flapping in the breeze implies hanging outside to dry. Reject unrelated locations (e.g. 'in a wardrobe/drawer', which wouldn't flap in a breeze).

questions.prompt: What had Sam's mother made specially?
questions.passage:
"We can't both be pirates!" said Lisa.

"Well, I'm not changing," replied Sam. "My mother made this specially."
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'a pirate costume/outfit' — Sam is dressed as a pirate and refuses to change, referring to what his mother made. Reject unrelated items.

questions.prompt: What sort of tree was it?
questions.passage:
Rhys looked at the tree longingly.

"Let me be next," he said in his head. And sure enough, the next gift was for him.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'a Christmas tree' — gifts placed near/under a tree and given out one at a time is a classic Christmas scene. Reject unrelated tree types with no connection to gift-giving.

questions.prompt: Why did Melissa pull her hat down?
questions.passage:
Melissa looked back over her shoulder and saw the thick, dark clouds moving towards her. She heard the rustling leaves in the trees and pulled her new red hat down firmly on her head.

The bag on her bike was. still half full. Melissa pedalled as hard as she could, quickly pushing morning papers into mail boxes.

At last she was almost finished. She just had to cross the bridge then make the long ride up Riverside Street.

Her bag now empty, her legs tired and sore, Melissa turned her bike around. She freewheeled down Riverside Street towards home. The clouds were almost overhead but there was no rain yet, just wind. Melissa tried to grab her hat, but it had gone. She last saw it sailing over the side of the bridge. Then the rain came.
questions.markingGuide: Accept answers referencing wind/an approaching storm threatening to blow her hat off (e.g. 'because it was windy', 'so it wouldn't blow away', evidenced by 'rustling leaves in the trees'). Reject answers with no connection to wind/weather (e.g. attributing it to keeping newspapers dry — that is not the stated reason for pulling the hat down).
